subject: history_social
passage: Empress Market, which opened in Karachi in 1889, was named for Queen Victoria and built around a large courtyard where traders sold grain, vegetables, and spices. Its most visible feature is a clock tower some 40 meters ______ a landmark that has stood over the crowded streets of the surrounding district for more than a century. The market is still busy today, and the tower remains one of the best-known sights of the old city.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "A landmark that has stood over the crowded streets … for more than a century" is not a sentence; it is a phrase that renames the clock tower. Such a phrase is attached to the end of a sentence with a comma.
explanation.A: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the describing phrase runs into "high" with nothing to connect it to the tower.
explanation.B: Correct. The comma attaches the phrase that renames the clock tower to the end of the sentence.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "A landmark that has stood over the crowded streets" contains only a "that" clause and no main verb, so it can't stand as a sentence; this creates a fragment.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A semicolon must have an independent clause on each side; the describing phrase is not a clause.
